statement (FES-74-8) prepared by the Bureau of Indian Affairs and entitled "Crow Ceded Area Coal Lease, Westmoreland Resources Mining Proposal" more specifically discusses the present coal mining operation. This statement was made available to the Council on Environmental Quality and the Public January 29, 1974.
Existing Mining Operations
Westmoreland Resources operates the Absaloka Mine on Tract III.

The mine is located in secs. 25 and 26, T. 1 N., R. 37 E. and currently employs a work force of about 110 persons. The Rosebud-McKay, Robinson and Stray-2 seam are currently mined. Limited mining of the Stray-1 seam has also taken place.
The mining plan for the 770 acre site was approved in early 1974 (See Map No. I-3). Site construction for the present coal mining operation began in October, 1972 and surface coal mining operations commenced in the spring of 1974. A 36 mile railroad spur line was built along Sarpy Creek to connect the mine site with the main Burlington Northern line near Sanders, Montana. The first unit train of coal was loaded on July 1, 1974 with coal being shipped from the Tract III, Sarpy Creek mine by rail to the Minneapolis/St. Paul area of Minnesota. Coal shipments in 1975 totalled 4 million tons. Limited operating space within the currently approved mining plan will eventually limit Westmoreland's ability to meet train schedules. Limited working space also results in decreased recovery at the ends of the pits. These problems are expected to become much more acute by early 1977, necessitating a shift in mining operations.
